CRYPTO NEWS — August 4, 2026

Extreme Fear grips the market as BTC consolidates in the $62k–$64k range on light leverage and zero conviction. Alts are rotting faster than BTC—ETH down 1.20% weekly while SOL holds up slightly—signaling fragile breadth beneath the surface. Stablecoin reserves are loaded (US$ 255B+) but no one's buying the dip with conviction. Risk-off sentiment intensifies as regulatory momentum stalls and DeFi tailwinds show limits. This is capitulation territory, not reversal. Watch for a break above $64.1k or below $62.4k to confirm direction in the next 48h.

TODAY'S HIGHLIGHTS

Coldcard Wallet Bleeding Exits as Third Wave of Thefts Escalates
Galaxy Research confirms a third wave of thefts from Coldcard Bitcoin wallets has pushed observed losses to roughly 1,367 BTC—roughly $86M at current spot. The Coldcard CEO denied device-level vulnerability, but the pattern is clear: dormant single-sig addresses are hemorrhaging sats. WHAT THIS MEANS: Hardware wallet risk is real again. If you're holding cold storage on older single-signature setups, assume they're compromised unless you're rotating keys. This is a migration catalyst for multi-sig and institutional setups, but retail panic selling could add downside pressure in the near term.

DeFi Lending Posts First Monthly Rebound Since May, But It Won't Save This Market
DeFi lending recorded its first monthly growth in 2026, with active loans increasing 7.2% from $20.7 billion to $22.2 billion after five consecutive months of decline. Aave and Morpho continue consolidating the juice—two protocols now account for roughly two-thirds of all DeFi borrows. The macro catalyst was mostly ETH's 20% July gain, not fresh liquidity. WHAT THIS MEANS: The rebound is technical relief, not a structural fix. Stablecoin supply actually *contracted* 0.6% to US$ 312B in July despite lending growth—meaning the market is recycling existing capital, not drawing new money. DeFi traders can take the bounce, but don't mistake healing for healthy.

Morgan Stanley Slashes Circle Price Target 64% as USDC Contraction Signals Stablecoin Wars Heating Up
Morgan Stanley downgraded Circle Internet Group from Equalweight to Underweight with a price target slashed to $38.00 from $106.00. The bank cut forecasts for supply of the company's USDC stablecoin through 2028, citing weaker reserve income and lower-margin revenue. Competitive threats from tokenized money market funds and Open USD (backed by Visa, Mastercard, BlackRock, Coinbase) are eroding Circle's moat. WHAT THIS MEANS: This isn't just sell-side posturing—it's a watershed moment for stablecoin economics. USDC supply dropped to US$ 73B (down from $77B), and if Circle loses reserve income while defending market share through lower fees, margin compression is real. For traders: USDT and newer stablecoin models will see flight capital. For hodlers: watch Circle's Aug 5 earnings closely—if they miss on deposit volumes again, expect continued downside flow into competitors.

WATCH LIST

BTC directional break critical in next 24–48h. Hold above $63.5k support or risk test of $61k. ETH's weekly weakness against BTC remains a red flag—broad altcoin weakness suggests sentiment fragility despite modest day gains. Clarity Act stalls as Senate recess approaches (Aug 7 deadline); any regulatory disappointment this week could trigger coordinated short covering followed by capitulation selling. Monitor funding rates: all three major assets (BTC, ETH, SOL) hold neutral positioning—no squeeze setup, only dry-powder. Stablecoin inflows matter more than price action right now; watch for a $260B+ daily inflow to signal institutional re-entry; below $250B is further deterioration risk.

See you tomorrow — stay sharp, the consolidation's a setup, not a bottom.
